A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Retained content can be matched reliably across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization-error correlations, activation-patching experiments, early-exiting analyses, perplexities, and PopQA accuracy results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds GPTQ configuration comparisons, technical-domain results, an alternative-metric comparison, and topic analysis.

M1.justification: The studied quantizers, model architectures, early-exiting procedure, and cross-model activation patching remain unchanged. The additions concern supplementary evaluation and analysis rather than a revised proposed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds inter-method error-correlation evaluations on ArXiv and OpenWebMath using Llama3-70B. This extends coverage to technical text while retaining the existing FineWeb, WikiText, PopQA, and calibration datasets.

E2.justification: GPTQ, AWQ, NormalFloat, and EfficientQAT remain the evaluated quantization methods, with unchanged comparator membership in retained comparisons. The new GPTQ sweep varies existing-method settings; the topic classifier is an analysis tool, not a competing quantizer.

E3.justification: v2 adds GPTQ configurations with damping values 0.005, 0.01, and 0.02 using activation sorting, plus a 0.01 configuration without sorting. It also evaluates KL-based errors and applies a 24-topic classifier. Existing dataset splits, model sizes, and primary evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens the diagnostic analyses: Section 4.1 and Table 7 test GPTQ configuration sensitivity, Appendix A checks dependence on the error definition using KL divergence, and Section 7.1 adds automatic topic categorization and manual inspection. These address distinct robustness and data-characterization questions beyond v1's retained localization and long-tail analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added correlations are concrete results, not uncertainty estimates. Naming Pearson's kurtosis in revised captions clarifies the formula already present in v1.

E6.justification: Retained numerical tables and appendix plots are unchanged. New supplementary results include GPTQ-variant correlations of 0.92–0.95, average correlations of 0.69 on ArXiv and 0.89 on OpenWebMath, NLL/KL error agreement of at least 0.97, and topic proportions in Figure 3.

T1.justification: Appendix A introduces an alternative definition of quantization error as KL divergence from the full-precision distribution to the quantized distribution. Existing equations and mathematical reasoning remain unchanged; the new notation table consolidates existing definitions.

C1.justification: The introduction adds the claim that large-error examples cover diverse topics and expands the contribution framing to what data cause errors. The central claims about correlated errors, residual magnitudes, RMSNorm, and MLP gates remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds a rationale for choosing FineWeb because it is not used for calibration, interprets large-error examples as topically diverse and not unusual, and justifies retaining NLL-based errors through agreement with KL and lower computational cost. The main mechanism explanations and stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link, the topic-classifier identifier, default GPTQ activation-sorting and damping settings, and the exact English C4 calibration shard. These improve documented reproducibility without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: Five references are added, supporting GPTQ configuration analysis, topic classification, technical corpora, and outlier removal: Chen et al. (2025), Wettig et al. (2025), Azerbayev et al. (2023), Paster et al. (2023), and Luo et al. (2025). The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Section 7 becomes 'What Data Cause Large Errors?', with a new topic-analysis subsection and the original long-tail discussion moved into Section 7.2. The introduction and appendix headings receive limited revisions, and acknowledgements are added; most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a topic-distribution figure, notation table, and GPTQ-variant table; annotates Figure 2 with a zoomed inset; and restyles several main tables with colored columns. It merges v1 Tables 6–7 into a reformatted Table 8. The merged caption introduces an inconsistent 'descending' ranking description despite unchanged small-rank, small-weight entries.

improvement.justification: The added configuration, domain, and metric checks strengthen support for the retained findings, while topic characterization and new technical and code-access information improve usefulness and reproducibility documentation. These are modest gains, with the main results and limitations unchanged. They outweigh the localized Table 8 caption regression concerning ranking direction.
